No Signal Home
By John Googol

Type HELP for instructions.

Tug Cargo Hold

Dark — but a strobing red light pulses from somewhere aft. Cold. You've been sleeping in the gap between two shipping containers. A proximity alarm screams from the cockpit, aft of here.

You can see flashlight, ration bar, shipping crates, bedroll, datapad here.
The proximity alarm screams from the cockpit. Aft. Move.

Taken.
The proximity alarm screams from the cockpit. Aft. Move.

Taken.
The proximity alarm screams from the cockpit. Aft. Move.

You are carrying:
  flashlight, ration bar
The proximity alarm screams from the cockpit. Aft. Move.

Tug Cockpit

A cramped cockpit. Instruments flash amber — the proximity alarm fills the space with noise. Through the viewport, something massive and dark. Your fuel gauge reads three percent.

You can see airlock door, instrument panels, tug viewport, alarm button, docking controls, fuel gauge, comms system, pilot's seat here.
The alarm fills your head. The button — the big red one on the console — silence it first.
commands.comment: # Opening sequence — dock with The Stillwater

commands.output:
You slam the button. The alarm cuts off mid-shriek.

Silence. Your ears ring.

Through the viewport: a hull. Massive. Dark. Close. Getting closer. The nav computer identifies it: "STILLWATER — Meridian Solutions — STATUS: DERELICT."

Your fuel reads three percent. You can't divert. Can't outrun it. But a derelict this size — for a salvager, that's opportunity. If you can dock before the drift carries you into it.

Manual docking controls — joystick, throttle, and a bank of status indicators. Standard salvage rig setup. You know this.

Sequence: MANEUVER to take control, then CONNECT to extend the docking arm, then SEAL to pressurize.

You grab the joystick and bring the tug's thrusters online. Manual control engaged.

The Stillwater's hull slides across the viewport as you align with a docking port. Closing distance. You could brake to slow the approach, or go straight to connecting the arm.

You fire the reverse thrusters. The tug shudders and decelerates. Approach speed drops to a crawl.

Good. Controlled approach. The docking port is dead ahead.

You extend the docking arm. Magnetic clamps engage with a deep clunk that reverberates through the hull. Locked on.

The connection reads solid. You could check the pressure readings before sealing, or just seal it and go.

You pull up the pressure diagnostic. Atmosphere on the other side reads... breathable. Barely. The seal integrity shows green across the board.

Good practice. Ready to seal.

You activate the sealing mechanism. The airlock pressurizes with a deep hiss. Green across the board.

The airlock door unlocks. Aft leads to The Stillwater.

Airlock

A cylindrical airlock chamber connecting the tug to The Stillwater. Biohazard warning decals peel from the inner hull. Emergency lighting casts everything in pale amber. The tug is fore. The ship corridor stretches aft.

You can see biohazard sign, emergency locker, inspection window, claw marks here.
"BIOHAZARD CONTAINMENT PROTOCOLS IN EFFECT. Report symptoms to your supervisor. Meridian Solutions cares about your wellbeing."

Forward Corridor

A long corridor running through the bow of The Stillwater. Overhead pipes drip condensation. The air smells of machine oil and something faintly chemical. The airlock is fore. The corridor continues aft toward the cargo bay. A maintenance hatch opens to starboard.

You can see overhead pipes, floor panel here.

A loose floor panel. Beneath it, cables snake into darkness.
A deep crack reverberates through the deck. The ship shudders.

Behind you — from the airlock — a hiss of escaping atmosphere. The seal between the tug and The Stillwater is failing. You hear metal stress and pop.

Through the airlock inspection window: your tug, still docked. But the seal is compromised. Going back that way without a spacesuit would be suicide.

Cargo Bay

A cavernous cargo bay with high ceilings lost in shadow. Shipping containers stand in rows, some pried open. Someone has made a camp here — improvised bedding, a makeshift barricade of crates. The corridor is fore. A sealed bulkhead leads aft to the cargo hold. Storage is to starboard.

You can see cargo hold bulkhead, shipping containers, improvised bedding, makeshift barricade, Okafor here.
"You're in my bay." Okafor steps out from behind a container, arms folded. "Corporate? Crew?" A hard stare. "Or something else?"

Storage Annex

A supply room lined with industrial shelving. Spare parts, sealed ration containers, and maintenance equipment fill the racks. A yellow hazmat suit hangs from a hook near the door. The cargo bay is to port.

You can see hazmat suit, elevator parts, fabricator parts, weapons crate, industrial shelving here.
Taken.

A long corridor running through the bow of The Stillwater. Overhead pipes drip condensation. The air smells of machine oil and something faintly chemical. The airlock is fore. The corridor continues aft toward the cargo bay. A maintenance hatch opens to starboard.

You can see overhead pipes, floor panel here.
The hull groans — a deep structural sound. The ship settling, or something shifting in the dark.

Lower Mid Corridor

A junction point where the forward and aft sections meet. Direction signs point fore and aft, their corporate fonts cheerful against the grimy walls. A ladder leads up through a ceiling hatch. The corridor runs fore and aft. An elevator alcove opens to starboard.

You can see direction signs, elevator here.
A freight elevator leading down to the cryo deck. The control panel is dead — the motor assembly has failed.

Central Junction

A wide junction where the mid deck splits into two wings. Corporate signage directs crew to port for labs and medical, starboard for habitation. A Meridian Solutions poster reads: "People First. Profit Always." Ladders lead up and down.

You can see corporate signage here.

Lab Corridor

A corridor that was once sterile white, now streaked with grime. An old chemical spill has dried to a dark stain on the deck. A safety station with eye wash and gloves sits beside the door. The junction is to starboard. The science lab is to port. Medbay is aft.

You can see chemical spill, safety station here.

Science Lab

Workbenches cluttered with broken equipment — a centrifuge tipped on its side, an analyzer with a cracked display. Sealed sample containers line one shelf. A research terminal flickers in the corner, its screen half-corrupted. The corridor is to starboard.

You can see research terminal, sample containers here.

You can see chemical spill, safety station here.

Medbay

A medical facility with treatment beds and overhead surgical lights, all dead. A quarantine cell stands in the corner — its door bent outward from inside. Medical supply cabinets line the wall, most ransacked. The lab corridor is fore.

You can see medkit, quarantine cell, patient logs here.

Hab Corridor

The habitation wing. Warmer here, more human. Crew photos line the wall in mismatched frames. A bulletin board holds shift schedules and personal notices — one reads "DO NOT TRUST THE SYSTEM" in hasty marker. The junction is to port. The mess hall is to starboard. The library is aft.

You can see crew photos, bulletin board here.

Mess Hall

Long tables bolted to the deck. A food fabrication unit sits against the far wall, dark and silent. Corporate propaganda posters decorate every surface. Coffee mugs with crew names sit abandoned. The hab corridor is to port.

You can see food fabrication unit, propaganda posters, crew mugs here.

The habitation wing. Warmer here, more human. Crew photos line the wall in mismatched frames. A bulletin board holds shift schedules and personal notices — one reads "DO NOT TRUST THE SYSTEM" in hasty marker. The junction is to port. The mess hall is to starboard. The library is aft.

You can see crew photos, bulletin board here.
A terminal you haven't seen active before flickers to life nearby. SOMS is expanding its reach.

Library

The ship's data archive. Racks of physical media storage — data crystals, backup drives — fill metal shelving. A comfortable reading chair faces a large terminal display. This feels like the ship's memory. The hab corridor is fore.

You can see archive terminal, data storage racks, Lis, SOMS terminal here.
"Oh." Lis blinks, confused. "I didn't — I thought I was going to storage." A pause. A head tilt. "How can I help you?"

The habitation wing. Warmer here, more human. Crew photos line the wall in mismatched frames. A bulletin board holds shift schedules and personal notices — one reads "DO NOT TRUST THE SYSTEM" in hasty marker. The junction is to port. The mess hall is to starboard. The library is aft.

A wide junction where the mid deck splits into two wings. Corporate signage directs crew to port for labs and medical, starboard for habitation. A Meridian Solutions poster reads: "People First. Profit Always." Ladders lead up and down.

You can see corporate signage here.
Reed grabs your arm, eyes clear and desperate. "Listen to me. Something's in me. It's been in me since before you arrived. Don't let it — don't let me —" Their eyes cloud. The moment passes.

Upper Corridor

A narrow corridor with a low ceiling — submarine-tight. Ship schematics are posted behind scratched plexiglass. An intercom panel is mounted by the ladder. Crew bunks are aft. The captain's cabin is to starboard. The bridge is fore, behind a heavy security door.

You can see bridge door, ship schematics, intercom panel here.
The hull groans — a deep structural sound. The ship settling, or something shifting in the dark.

Crew Bunks

Stacked sleeping pods, four high. Most are stripped bare. One bunk has deep scratches gouged into the wall beside it. Dark stains on the mattress. A security rack holds equipment near the door. EVA suit storage is recessed into the far wall. The corridor is fore. The common area is aft.

You can see stun baton, EVA suit, scratched bunk, security rack, EVA storage here.

Common Area

A cramped recreation space. A viewport looks out into black nothing. Someone has built a barricade from furniture and deck plates across the starboard side of the room. A half-finished card game is scattered on a table. An air vent grille is set into the ceiling. The crew bunks are fore.

You can see common viewport, furniture barricade, card game, air vent, Vasik here.
A voice from behind the barricade: "Stop. Who are you? You're not crew." A pause. "You're from the tug. The convict."

NO SIGNAL HOME — Commands:

Movement: FORE, AFT, PORT, STARBOARD, UP, DOWN (or F, A, P, SB, U, D)
Actions: LOOK, EXAMINE, TAKE, DROP, OPEN, CLOSE, UNLOCK, READ
Special: PRY, REPAIR, CUT, CONNECT, OVERRIDE, LAUNCH
NPCs: ASK [person] ABOUT [topic], TALK TO [person]
Terminals: QUERY [terminal] ABOUT [topic], USE [terminal]
Search: SEARCH [thing], LOOK UNDER [thing]
System: SAVE, RESTORE, UNDO, INVENTORY, SCORE

Tip: EXAMINE everything. Talk to everyone. Read every terminal.

NO SIGNAL HOME
A sci-fi salvage horror text adventure.

You are a grey-market salvager who drifted into range of The Stillwater, a derelict corporate freighter waking from the dead. Four survivors. One AI. Five possible endings.

By John Googol. Built with Sharpee.

Manual docking controls — joystick, throttle, and a bank of status indicators. Standard salvage rig setup. You know this.

You grab the joystick and bring the tug's thrusters online. Manual control engaged.

Good. Controlled approach. The docking port is dead ahead.

The connection reads solid. You could check the pressure readings before sealing, or just seal it and go.

You pull up the pressure diagnostic. Atmosphere on the other side reads... breathable. Barely. The seal integrity shows green across the board.

Good practice. Ready to seal.

Reed grabs your arm, eyes clear and desperate. "Listen to me. Something's in me. It's been in me since before you arrived. Don't let it — don't let me —" Their eyes cloud. The moment passes.

SOMS goes silent. Not dead — disabled. Contained.

The ship is yours now. The doors are open. The systems respond to your commands.

It's not over. Three hundred people in cryo. A pathogen in the hold. A military buyer waiting at Korvax Station.

But for the first time since you boarded, the ship is quiet. Really quiet.

You sit in the captain's chair and think about what comes next.
